chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about branding livestock, and he said: There is no problem with it, except on their faces.

key_terms.الْمَوَاشِي: Livestock; domesticated animals kept for agricultural or commercial purposes (cattle, sheep, camels, horses)
key_terms.سِمَة: Branding mark; the act of marking animals with a hot iron for identification purposes
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/harm; a standard jurisprudential phrase indicating permissibility (ibaha)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to brand livestock in Islam?
ai.summary: The narrator Abdullah ibn Sinan posed a question to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the Islamic ruling on branding livestock with identifying marks. The Imam responded that such branding is permissible without restriction, with a single exception: branding on the animals' faces is prohibited. This ruling reflects the Islamic ethical principle of avoiding unnecessary harm and pain to animals, particularly in sensitive areas like the face.
